Mr. S.C. Dumka, A.G.A. and Mr. Nikhil
Bisht, Brief Holder for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Mohd. Matlub, Advocate has put in
appearance on behalf of the complainant.
2. By means of the present application, the
applicant seeks grant of anticipatory bail in
connection with F.I.R./Case Crime No.0247 of
2026, registered at Police Station Jaspur,
District Udham Singh Nagar, for the offence
punishable under Sections 109(1), 117(2),
191(2), 191(3), 3(5), 351(3) & 352 of B.N.S.,
2023.
3. As per the contents of the F.I.R., the
applicant alongwith co-accused assaulted the
injured and in the F.I.R., role of the applicant
has been specifically assigned that he tried to
runover his Black Coloured Venue Car, bearing
registration No.UK18R-9495, which he was
driving over the injured Mohsin, due to which
he suffered injuries in his spinal cord.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant
submits that applicant has falsely been
implicated in the instant case. He submits that
applicant is nowhere visible in the CCTV
footage. He submits that applicant has been
merely implicated due to previous dispute

UKHC010154552026
2026:UHC:7877
between the parties. He submits that neither
the applicant is owner of the aforesaid Venue
Car nor the same was driven by the applicant.
It is, therefore, prayed that applicant be
granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.
5. Learned State Counsel, on written
instructions received from the Investigating
Officer, submits that the presence of the
applicant at the place of incident is verified by
the Investigating Officer by examining the
CCTV cameras installed at the place of
incident. He submits that applicant is not
cooperating in the investigation, as such,
proceedings under Section 84 of B.N.S.S. has
been initiated against him. The written
instructions are taken on record.
6. Having heard learned counsel for the
applicant, learned State Counsel and the
learned counsel appearing for the complainant,
and upon perusal of the material brought on
record, this Court finds that the allegations
against the applicant are specific and serious in
nature. In the F.I.R., a specific role has been
attributed to the applicant of attempting to run
over the injured Mohsin with the black-coloured Venue car bearing registration No.
UK18R-9495, allegedly driven by him, resulting
in injuries to the injured, including injury to his
spinal cord. The contention of learned counsel
for the applicant that the applicant is not
visible in the CCTV footage and that he has
been falsely implicated on account of a previous
dispute between the parties, cannot, at this
stage, be accepted so as to extend the
discretionary relief of anticipatory bail. The
Investigating Officer, on the basis of the CCTV
footage collected during investigation, has
verified the presence of the applicant at the
place of occurrence. The defence set up by the
applicant, including the question as to who was
driving the aforesaid vehicle, involves
appreciation of the evidence and cannot be
conclusively examined at the stage of
consideration of an application for anticipatory
bail. It is further borne out from the
instructions received from the Investigating
Officer that the applicant has not been
cooperating with the investigation and,

UKHC010154552026
2026:UHC:7877
consequently, proceedings under Section 84 of
the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023,
have already been initiated against him. Non-cooperation with the investigation, coupled with
the specific role attributed to the applicant and
the nature and gravity of the allegations,
weighs against grant of anticipatory bail.
7. Having regard to the nature of the
accusations, the specific role assigned to the
applicant, the material collected during
investigation regarding his presence at the
place of occurrence, and his alleged non-cooperation with the investigating agency, this
Court is not inclined to exercise its
discretionary jurisdiction in favour of the
applicant.
8. Accordingly, the present Anticipatory Bail
Application is dismissed.
 (Alok Mahra, J.) 02.09.2026
